specSource: ~/code/product-owner/stories/yield-claim-nft/review/yield-claim-nft-Balancexit/052-unipooler-cutover-escrow.md (Design > Access); restated in contract NatSpec L63-65
description: The operator gate stops one front-run variant: a stranger calling exitAndSeed first, which would seed the pair and make the owner's later exitAndSeed revert PairNotEmpty. It does not stop the cheaper variant, which needs no call to the escrow at all: a Balancer swap that moves either side of the proportional share by more than the floor tolerance. Econ fork-proved this at the repo's 1 bp tolerance. A 4 sUSDS->phUSD swap makes exitAndSeed revert AmountOutBelowMin(phUSD, 22,453.35e18, 22,454.12e18), at a round-trip cost of about $0.03 at that 1 bp tolerance (tolerance-dependent; see L-28). story-103 broadcasts through the public mempool (`--broadcast --skip-simulation --slow --ledger --legacy`, 103 L99) as separate transactions, and the floors are quoted before the broadcast. So the gate does not deliver the full mid-cutover-revert protection the story implies. Organic Balancer flow can trip the same check.
deviation: The code is faithful to the design. The story's rationale for that design is incomplete: the gate does prevent the variant it names (a stranger calling exitAndSeed or abort first), but the story implies it protects the broadcast from mid-cutover reverts, and a gate-independent vector (a Balancer swap past a tight floor) remains. The 'tight tolerance' itself comes from the runbook (phStaging2 docs/BalancerWinddownPlan.md L385) and the story-052 L194 fork-test spec, not from the access rationale. Law-1 assessment: the story's intent is not unsafe. The transaction is atomic, the BPT stays in the escrow, and the operator can re-quote and retry or abort() to the old pooler, so no value can be extracted (ECON-001 shows a sandwich within the floors is net-negative for the attacker). The residual is liveness only, so this is not escalated as story-unsafe. Spec correction: the story and the 103 runbook should state that floor-tolerance reverts are expected and recoverable, and that the tolerance should be sized for griefing resistance rather than 'tight' (plan L385). ECON-001 shows a loose floor gives up no value on two constant-product venues. The runbook should also say how the progress file resumes after an exitAndSeed revert.
